entries.content_plain:
Introduction

 Solomon having ended his prayer, the fire of the Lord comes down from heaven and consumes the offerings, 2Chr 7:1 . The people and the priests see this, and glorify God, and offer sacrifices, 2Chr 7:2-4 . Solomon offers twenty-two thousand oxen, and one hundred and twenty thousand sheep; and the priests and Levites attend in their offices, 2Chr 7:5 , 2Chr 7:6 . He keeps the feast seven days, and the dedication of the altar seven days, and dismisses the people, 2Chr 7:7-11 . The Lord appears unto him by night, and assures him that he has heard his prayer, 2Chr 7:12-16 ; promises him and his posterity a perpetual government, if they be obedient, 2Chr 7:17 , 2Chr 7:18 ; but utter destruction should they disobey, and become idolaters, 2Chr 7:19-22 . 

 Verse 1 

 The fire came down - The cloud had come down before, now the fire consumes the sacrifice, showing that both the house and the sacrifices were accepted by the Lord.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 10</hi> <div eID="gen14050" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14051" type="x-p"/> On the three and twentieth day - This was the ninth day of the dedication of the temple; but in <reference osisRef="1Kgs.8.66">1Kgs 8:66</reference> it is called the eighth day. "The meaning is this," says Jarchi: "he gave them liberty to return on the eighth day, and many of them did then return: and he dismissed the remainder on the ninth, what is called here the twenty-third, reckoning the fourteen days for the duration of the two feasts; in all, twenty-three." <div eID="gen14051" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14052" type="x-p"/> The Targum paraphrases this verse thus: "The people departed with a glad heart, for all the good which God had done to David his servant, on whose account the doors of the sanctuary were open and for Solomon his son, because God had heard his prayer, and the majesty of the Lord had rested on the house of the sanctuary and for Israel, his people, because God had favourably accepted their oblations, and the heavenly fire had descended, and, burning on the altar, had devoured their sacrifices."
